textbookBox.concept: A joint family has several generations living together: grandparents, parents, uncles, aunts, brothers, sisters and cousins. A nuclear family has only parents and children.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: A joint family has several generations living together: grandparents, parents, uncles, aunts, brothers, sisters and cousins. A nuclear family has only parents and children.
beats.speakEn: A joint family has several generations living together: grandparents, parents, uncles, aunts, brothers, sisters and cousins. A nuclear family has only parents and children.

beats.en: Family relationships are based on love, care, cooperation and interdependence. Grandparents tell stories with humour and wisdom, parents provide and guide, and children help at home as they grow.

textbookBox.concept: A group of connected people who live in the same area or share work or interests may be called a community. We belong to many communities: neighbourhood, school, clubs and groups of friends.

beats.en: A group of connected people who live in the same area or share work or interests may be called a community. We belong to many communities: neighbourhood, school, clubs and groups of friends.
beats.speakEn: A group of connected people who live in the same area or share work or interests may be called a community. We belong to many communities: neighbourhood, school, clubs and groups of friends.

beats.en: Kamal Parmar, who ran a small workshop in Ahmedabad, noticed children on the street who did not go to school. He started classes for them, 150 children joined regularly and older students volunteered as teachers.
